comment: Suzuki sensei is an amazing professor and you will learn so much Japanese in such a short amount of time. His class is truly rewarding and he wants everyone to succeed. That being said, I have more work for this class than any class I have taken before. Prepare to spend at least an hour a night studying to be prepared for drill classes!

You WILL learn Japanese if you take Suzuki Sensei's class and take it seriously, but there's a catch. For my Computer Scientists: in any given week, I'd do more homework for JAP101 than I did in CMSC 315. Amazing curriculum if you're ready to grind, but he demands *a lot* from you outside the classroom.
Very tough Sensei, but the most rewarding language class I have taken at the University of Richmond. Absolutely incredible professor, and will absolutely reward hard work.

One of the best professors at Richmond for sure. His classes are not incredibly difficult if you make sure to prepare before each one. In my opinion, his intensity is part of his charm. He comes off as intense simply because he really wants you to do well, so don't be too scared away if he seems too intense at first.

Suzuki-sensei really cares about you learning his mother tongue. He's getting old but nonetheless he is really passionate, but just requires you to be patient sometimes and make sure to speak up since his hearing is not as good. Do the studying and it will pay off in his class, he really knows how to teach a language well.

Suzuki sensei is the best teacher at UR hands down.  He is very intense at first, and has high expectations that you study a good amount outside of class, at least enough to know the vocab, but the further you get into Japanese the more you will love him.  He reaches out to students who seem to be struggling and truly wants everyone to do great.

Basically just expects you to memorize his book. His lecture are super convoluted because he barely speaks English. He speaks down on everyone and its really annoying. He doesnt like criticism so if you disagree with him he wont hesitate to humiliate you in front of the class.

He barely grades anything from 101-202. The TA does it. His lectures are unclear because 1) he doesnt speak English and 2) he expects you to learn from the textbook that HE wrote. He would often publicly humiliate his students. Asking him for advice or any questions that he considers dumb will end with you being berated. Hes a terrible person.

Suzuki overall is a great guy. He takes the baptism by fire approach to weed out students in the beginning but once you get to know him and the class gets smaller he will ease up. Even though I struggled with the course material as I got to the higher level classes, he was pretty forgivable with the grading.

Suzuki sensei is an inspiration with a great passion for language and his students. He has vast knowledge on the different origins of certain grammatical points, words, kanji, etc, and you can truly learn a lot about the Japanese language from him even outside of what he directly offers in his curriculum. His class is hard, but definitely worth it!

Suzuki sensei is truly caring & funny. I love him to bits & pieces. If youre facing difficulty in the class, please understand that a) Japanese is not an Indo-European language & b) this class is designed to be hard so you ACTUALLY learn the language! I can't believe people said he racially discriminates - I'm not Asian & he has been plenty caring

Very caring and funny behind his sarcasm (sometimes at the students' expense). Uses his own (uninspiring) textbook and teaches in a non-mainstream way, hurting prior learners. Drills are very frequent and pretty intense and grades aren't calculated until the end. If you're passionate, go for it; just study and try not to fall behind or you'll drown
Suzuki sensei is really willing to answer your questions in class and after class. He is responsible for his teaching and your grades if you let him know your hard work.

Currently taking Japanese 101 with Suzuki-sensei. In a class with 8 students, and it has evolved over the months from a scary new environment to a warm, welcoming family. He cares quietly about each student's well being He teaches with pride and excellence, and if you work hard you will be rewarded. If you are bad at stress/time management, avoid!

Now fluent, married, living in Japan, I understand Prof. Suzuki so well. He's tough and there's a lot of drilling/memorization, but this is how you learn Japanese. Japanese culture values hard work with little recognition. Students who expect to be pampered and coddled will not survive and shouldn't take this class. Truly my favorite professor ever

I am reflecting on this class after graduating 10 years ago. I still clearly remember everything about the course and the guidance given to us by Suzuki Sensei. If you invest in his class w/ genuine interest and an effort to learn, he will invest even more into you. Because of him, I am fluent in Japanese and have a career and life in Japan.

I have taken Japanese for 5 years prior this course. As of now I have actually quit Japanese and switched to another language. Very hard grader, very stubborn, very unwilling to compromise. He doesn't acknowledge that the English language is very different than Japanese in the sense that it has so many more exception and variation. Beware.

He tries tries very hard to help you learn, but you need to put major time in out of class to get a good grade.  Nothing against him personally, but the class is really hard and he expectations for you are set very high.
Awesome teacher. It feels like your brain is going to explode after one drill class, however you learn a lot. Try your best and he will like you.

Students should be grateful to have such an attentive and hard working teacher. He does not play favorites but only calls out those WHO DO NOT WORK. So I think those who have negative things to say do not belong in his class and have delusions about their own Japanese ability. Japanese is a difficult language and Suzuki Sensei is the best teacher.

He did not let my place out of Japanese, which is a waste of my time. He criticizes a lot of other methods of teaching japanese, which i think is wrong.  He is a great person, but okay teacher.  If you are going to take japanese for the 1st time, it will be tough and he will be harsh. he calls everyone out, but has his favorites

If the idea of taking Japanese intimidates you, don't take this class. If you're open to learning something entirely new, then take the class. It's hard. There are new things to learn every week and success only comes with constant practice. Fairly easy/decent grader.

Prof. Suzuki is a great teacher who really knows his stuff.  He cares for the success of all of his students and is a very meticulous, fair grader.  A lot of people think the class is hard, but that's more owing to the subject rather than the instructor.

First, I was surprised at ANY negative comments. I want to say  that I am working in Japan BECAUSE of Prof. Suzuki. Japanese is a hard language and I think people should work hard in his class. Those who rate him lowly always have a problem with doing real work!  If you want no work you do not belong in class or JAPAN! There is NO discrimination.

This professor is by far the worst I ever had.  If you want to take Japanese 101 make sure you've either taken a japanese class before or you are an asian (he will not hesitate to discriminate).  Don't put it past him to mock you.  He calls you out too.  I worked harder in this class than every other class combined and ended up with a D+ DONT TAKE!

This class was probably one of the most enjoyable that I have ever taken.  The teacher doesn't necessarily explain things perfectly the first time, however he will literally cut into quiz time (and make it a take-home) so as he can ensure that the students understand the content. I would also recommend this class to anyone with an interest in jap.

Difficult, but once you prove to him that you really want to learn and are not going to drop out, he takes a genuine interest in your well being, which is great. Really one of if the not The best instructor at any grade level that I've ever had. He picks on me constantly. It's awesome :D

I'm not sure why some commentors would put some of the things they have. Not only is Suzuki incredibly engaged in his class, but it is genuinely fun. I've had a great time and would encourage anybody who has even a little interest to take this class. You have to do some work, but if you're interested none of it is hard.

Very hard teacher, does not care about the students, requires to much work and expects you to learn grammer on your own. If you go to his office hours, he doesnt help he talks to you for 5 mins and then the conversation is over. Do not take this class I came in with taking jap in high school and i struggled

You must put in a lot of effort in this class.  I hate the book. I hate his style of drill class.  Try hard, especially with speaking, and you will learn a bit, but you must go to Japan to really grasp the language.  Also, not a particularly cool professor.  good luck.
you must try hard in this class.  do not let him down.  He likes to teach students who care.  Book sucks.
very hard and moves at an incredibly fast pass.  its the most stressful class with the highest expectations I've had.  However, he is a fantastic teacher despite the demand.
demanding teacher.  He likes teaching but don't let him down.  Put lots of effort into class and you'll get a lot out of it.

Teaches a really, really challenging class.  He is a good teacher, but I didn't like his agressive, answer-on-the-spot teaching methods.  Found his class to be distractingly stressful.  He also uses a terrible book which doesn't teach Kanji.
